In the morning I boiled some savory scorched rice and ate it.

You can hear warm, earthy dialect at the country market.

explain_en: 구수하다 is for flavors and smells like barley tea, scorched rice and soybean paste. 고소하다 is the nutty taste of sesame oil or nuts.

examples.en: The vegetables at the market are fresh.
The fish was so fresh that we ate it raw.

examples.ko: 싱싱한 과일을 사려고 아침 일찍 시장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the market early to buy fresh fruit.
The cucumbers are so fresh they taste good even eaten right away.
I bought flowers, and they are still fresh after two days.

explain: 싱싱하다는 채소, 과일, 생선, 꽃처럼 살아 있는 것의 느낌이 있어요. ‘신선한 공기’처럼 쓰는 신선하다와는 조금 달라요.

dict_examples.ko: 싱싱한 재료를 써야 음식이 맛있다.

dict_examples.en: In the mallow soup dried shrimp floated like bright red petals, the lettuce and crown daisy were fresh, and the pickled garlic was nicely fermented.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Just then Sanghui stopped working and went outside. Since Dohyeon had come after so long, she said she'd at least buy some fresh fruit.

explain_en: 싱싱하다 has the feeling of something alive and crisp, like vegetables, fruit, fish or flowers. It differs a bit from 신선하다, which also works for things like fresh air.

en: to be tender; to be light (color)

examples.en: The meat was really tender.
I like light sky-blue shirts.

examples.ko: 상추가 연해서 쌈 싸 먹기 좋아요.
examples.en: The lettuce is tender, so it's good for wraps.
A light pink lipstick suits you well.
Please make my coffee weak.

explain: 연하다의 반대말은 뜻에 따라 달라요. 고기는 질기다, 색이나 커피는 진하다예요.

explain_en: The opposite of 연하다 depends on the meaning. For meat it is 질기다 (tough); for colors or coffee it is 진하다 (strong, deep).

en: to be pretty, delicate (color, texture, manner)

examples.en: The colors in the painting are lovely.
My grandmother is old, but her skin is still lovely.

examples.ko: 고운 한복을 입은 아이들이 사진을 찍어요.
examples.en: Children in lovely hanbok are taking photos.
I walked barefoot on the fine sand.
My friend has a kind heart.

explain: 곱다는 ㅂ 불규칙이라 고와요, 고운으로 바뀌어요. 색, 피부, 마음씨처럼 곱고 부드러운 것에 써요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 곱게 자라서 힘든 일을 해 본 적이 없대요.
phrases.en: to be brought up gently, to grow up sheltered
phrases.nuance_en: to be raised preciously without hardship
phrases.en_equiv: to be brought up gently, to grow up sheltered

explain_en: 곱다 is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes 고와요 and 고운. It is used for soft, delicate things like colors, skin and a gentle heart.

en: to be hateful, to be detestable; to be annoying

examples.ko: 같은 실수를 또 한 제가 조금 미웠어요.
examples.en: I was a bit annoyed with myself for making the same mistake again.

examples.ko: 아기가 밤새 울어도 하나도 밉지 않아요.
examples.en: Even when the baby cries all night, I can't be mad at it at all.

examples.ko: 동생이 제 과자를 다 먹어서 미웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling ate all my snacks, so I was mad at them.

examples.ko: 친구가 약속을 또 어겨서 정말 미워요.
examples.en: My friend broke our plan again, and I'm really annoyed with them.
I envy people who can say things without sounding nasty.

explain: 밉다는 ㅂ 불규칙이라 미워요가 돼요. 사람을 미워하는 마음은 미워하다로 말해요. 친구를 미워해요 / 친구가 미워요.

phrases.en_equiv: a bond built through both the good and the bad times

phrases.en_equiv: the 'terrible sevens', a stubborn, defiant age

explain_en: 밉다 is ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes 미워요. To say you hate a person, use 미워하다: 친구를 미워해요 / 친구가 미워요.

examples.en: The moon is round tonight.

examples.ko: 둥근 식탁이라서 여섯 명이 같이 앉을 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a round table, so six people can sit together.
The Earth is round.
I baked round cookies.

examples.ko: 저 둥근 지붕이 있는 건물이 박물관이에요.
examples.en: The building with the round roof over there is the museum.

explain: 둥글다는 ㄹ이 빠져서 둥근이 돼요. 둥근 달. 큰 모양에는 둥글다를, 작고 귀여운 것에는 동그랗다를 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀장님은 성격이 둥글둥글해서 모두와 잘 지내요.

phrases.nuance_en: a personality with no sharp edges that gets along with everyone
phrases.en_equiv: to have an easygoing, agreeable personality

explain_en: 둥글다 drops the ㄹ and becomes 둥근. 둥근 달. People often use 둥글다 for bigger shapes and 동그랗다 for small, cute ones.

examples.en: The child's eyes went wide.
I cut colored paper into circles and made a card.
I put cheese on the round bread.
The baby's cheeks are round, so they're cute.
We sat in a circle with friends and talked.

explain: 동그랗다는 ㅎ 불규칙이에요. 동그래요, 동그란, 동그랗게로 바뀌어요. 하얗다 → 하얘요와 같아요.

dict_examples.ko: 동그란 안경.

dict_examples.ko: 동그란 얼굴 왼쪽 뺨에 까만 점이 귀엽다.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: He handed a coin to a place by the roadside where round bread was baked in a brazier.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 시해가 동그란 눈을 깜박이며 오빠를 올려다보았다.
dict_examples.en: Sihae blinked her round eyes and looked up at her older brother.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 동그랗게 등을 구부리고 콩밭에 앉아서 우묵댁이 울고 있었다.
dict_examples.en: Umukdaek sat in the bean field with her back curled round, crying.

explain_en: 동그랗다 is ㅎ-irregular: 동그래요, 동그란, 동그랗게. It works like 하얗다 → 하얘요.

examples.en: This exam's difficulty was similar to last time.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 난이도가 너무 높아서 금방 포기했어요.
examples.en: This game was way too hard, so I gave up quickly.

examples.ko: 게임을 시작할 때 난이도를 고를 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can choose the difficulty level when you start the game.

examples.ko: 난이도를 낮추면 초보자도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lower the difficulty, even beginners can do it.

examples.ko: 난이도에 따라 문제를 세 단계로 나눴어요.
examples.en: I divided the questions into three levels by difficulty.

explain: 난이도는 보통 높다/낮다와 함께 써요. “난이도가 어렵다”는 어색하게 들릴 수 있어요. “난이도가 높다”라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 난이도에 따라 단계적으로 교육하다.
dict_examples.en: To teach in stages according to difficulty level.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 시험 문제의 난이도를 조정하기가 쉽지 않다.
dict_examples.en: It isn't easy to adjust the difficulty of exam questions.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 시험 전체의 난이도는 모든 문항의 난이도를 합산하여 평균하면 산출된다.
dict_examples.en: The overall difficulty of an exam is calculated by summing and averaging the difficulty of all items.

dict_examples.ko: 하지만 입시 철에 교수 등이 한 달여간 합숙해 만들어 내는 문제는 난이도 조절에 실패할 가능성이 항상 있다.

explain_en: 난이도 normally goes with 높다/낮다 (high/low). “난이도가 어렵다” can sound awkward; say “난이도가 높다.”

examples.en: Satisfaction with the food was high, but the service wasn't great.

examples.ko: 고객 만족도 조사에 답하면 쿠폰을 줘요.
examples.en: If you answer the customer satisfaction survey, you get a coupon.
This app has a high user satisfaction level.
When employee satisfaction goes up, service gets better too.

examples.ko: 가격에 비해 만족도가 낮아서 다시 안 살 거예요.
examples.en: Satisfaction is low for the price, so I won't buy it again.

explain: -도는 ‘정도’라는 뜻이에요. 만족도, 난이도처럼 높다/낮다와 함께 써요.

dict_examples.ko: 만족도가 높다.

explain_en: -도 means “degree.” Words like 만족도 and 난이도 go together with 높다/낮다 (high/low).

examples.en: The night sky in the picture is very black.

examples.ko: 바닷가에서 하루 종일 놀아서 얼굴이 검게 탔어요.
examples.en: I played at the beach all day and got a deep tan.

examples.en: A round white moon is up in the sky.
I got kimchi juice on my white shirt.
Even just white rice and kimchi is delicious.
Grandma's hair is white like snow.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 피부가 희어서 햇빛에 쉽게 타요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has fair skin and burns easily in the sun.

explain: ‘흰 셔츠’처럼 흰은 아주 많이 써요. “희어요”도 맞지만 말할 때는 “하얘요”를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: 흰 is very common, as in ‘흰 셔츠’. “희어요” is correct too, but in speech you will often hear “하얘요” more.

examples.en: The teacher's explanation was detailed.
I'll send you the details by email.

examples.ko: 길을 자세하게 알려 줘서 쉽게 찾았어요.
examples.en: They gave me detailed directions, so I found it easily.
Read the contract carefully before signing.
The map was detailed, so I didn't get lost.

explain: 자세하다는 ‘자세’(posture)와 소리는 같지만 다른 단어예요. 자세히 알려 줘요 / 자세가 나빠요.
explain_en: 자세하다 sounds like 자세 (posture), but they are different words. 자세히 알려 줘요 (tell in detail) / 자세가 나빠요 (poor posture).
